canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: Both reviewers were right that the `/lh-attach` production path is broken and that the epic gate is hollow. I independently confirmed both issues in code and with live repros. Reviewer 1 also blocked on lifecycle auto-management before attach/import; I verified that too by emitting `session_start` against a pre-populated session file, which created a managed thread containing only a `runtime_event` and then caused `/lh-attach` to fail with `TARGET_ASSOCIATION_CONFLICT`, so there is no evidence to downgrade that blocker. The two reviewer descriptions of the attach bug were merged into one canonical finding that covers both missing active-branch context and wrong target association when an explicit session path is supplied. The synthetic import `sessionManager` adapter is real but currently observational, so it remains non-blocking.
crossStoryFindings: Story 2 lifecycle wiring and Story 5 attach/import semantics are inconsistent: live PI handlers auto-manage newly seen session targets, which prevents Story 5 from importing pre-existing history on those targets.

Story 5 `/lh-attach` and Story 7 `pi-session` fixture flows have drifted apart: fixture creation forwards the live `SessionManager` and `activeLeafId`, but attach does not, so the same branched session succeeds in one story surface and fails in the other.

The unit suite now protects the wrong session-switch behavior in `tests/context-steward/capture-service.test.ts:741-777`, while the planned command and integration layers that should have exercised `/lh-attach` at the production boundary are missing.
architectureFindings: `src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:563-617` contradicts `docs/spec-build/technical-architecture.md:372-375` by opening or creating a managed thread for every session lifecycle event instead of requiring attach/import for pre-populated or newly switched unmanaged sessions.

`src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:304-320` together with `src/context-steward/services/import-service.ts:276-302` violate the active-path import contract in `docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/tech-design.md:63` and the epic boundary contract in `docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/epic.md:581` by binding `/lh-attach` to the current session context rather than the requested import target.
`scripts/run-node-tests.mjs:39-43` conflicts with the epic test-plan gate in `docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/test-plan.md:221-235` by treating an empty integration suite as success.
epicCoverageAssessment: `npm run verify` passed with 104 unit tests, so the store, capture, import, repair, fixture, and helper service seams are broadly exercised.

Epic-level gate coverage is incomplete: the test plan requires `verify-all` plus `file-thread-store.integration.test.ts` smoke tests, but the repository has no `*.integration.test.ts` files and `npm run verify-all` completed after printing `No integration tests found.`

Command-surface coverage drift is real: the test plan lists `/lh-attach`, `/lh-turn-health`, `/lh-repair-turns`, `/lh-fixture`, and `/lh-status`, but `tests/context-steward/pi-extension-commands.test.ts` currently exercises only fixture and status flows plus formatter checks.
productionPathFindings: Reproduced: emitting `session_start` against a pre-populated PI session file created a managed thread whose only stored message was `runtime_event`; a follow-on `/lh-attach` then failed with `TARGET_ASSOCIATION_CONFLICT`.

Reproduced: `/lh-attach` on a branched live session returned `IMPORT_PATH_AMBIGUOUS ... expected exactly one leaf candidate but found 2`, while a direct `attachExistingPiSession` call using the live `sessionManager` and `activeLeafId` imported 3 messages from `leaf:branch-entry-002`.

Reproduced: `/lh-attach <other-session-file>` imported the other file's messages into a thread still targeted at the current live session id/path; the recorded `import.sourceSessionId` also followed the live session instead of the imported file header.
`npm run verify-all` passed only because `scripts/run-node-tests.mjs` exits 0 when the integration discovery set is empty, so the epic gate never exercises a real integration path.

blockingFindings.title: Lifecycle events auto-manage pre-populated or newly switched PI sessions before attach/import can preserve prior history
blockingFindings.evidence: `ensureActiveThread()` in `src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:563-579` calls `openOrCreateManagedThread({ target }, store)` before every `session_start`, `session_before_switch`, `session_shutdown`, `turn_start`, `turn_end`, and `message_end` handler (`:596-617`). `docs/spec-build/technical-architecture.md:372-375` instead says pre-populated sessions must be attached/imported before they are treated as managed and newly switched unmanaged sessions must require attach/import. Live repro: after `session_start` on a pre-populated session file, the created managed thread contained only `runtime_event`, and a subsequent `/lh-attach` failed with `TARGET_ASSOCIATION_CONFLICT`. `tests/context-steward/capture-service.test.ts:741-777` also asserts fresh auto-management whenever the target changes, so the wrong behavior is now protected by tests.

blockingFindings.title: `/lh-attach` drops live branch context and can bind imported history to the wrong PI session target
blockingFindings.evidence: `executeAttachCommand()` in `src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:304-320` forwards only `targetFromContext(ctx)` and `sessionFilePath`; it does not pass `activeLeafIdFromContext()` or `importSessionManagerFromContext()`, unlike `executeFixtureCommand()` at `src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:449-457`. `attachExistingPiSession()` then prefers `input.target.sessionId` and `input.target.sessionFilePath` over the command argument when building the managed target (`src/context-steward/services/import-service.ts:276-302`). This violates the active-path contract in `docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/tech-design.md:63` and the epic boundary contract that attach accepts a PI session path or identifier (`docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/epic.md:581`). Live repros: `/lh-attach` on a branched live session returned `IMPORT_PATH_AMBIGUOUS`, while direct `attachExistingPiSession({ activeLeafId, sessionManager })` imported 3 messages; `/lh-attach <other-session-file>` imported 3 messages into a thread still targeted at the current live session id/path and recorded the live session id as `import.sourceSessionId`.

blockingFindings.title: `verify-all` passes without the planned integration suite, so the epic gate is vacuous
blockingFindings.evidence: `docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/test-plan.md:221-235` defines `verify-all` as `npm run verify && npm run test:integration` and requires `file-thread-store.integration.test.ts` smoke coverage. The repository currently has no `*.integration.test.ts` files, and `scripts/run-node-tests.mjs:39-43` prints `No integration tests found.` and exits 0 when discovery is empty. I ran `npm run verify-all`; unit tests passed, then the integration phase exited successfully after that message, so the epic gate is presently hollow.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Planned command-surface coverage for attach, turn-health, and repair is missing
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/test-plan.md:181-185` expects command-surface tests for `/lh-attach`, `/lh-turn-health`, `/lh-repair-turns`, `/lh-fixture`, and `/lh-status`, but `tests/context-steward/pi-extension-commands.test.ts:88-221` covers formatter behavior, `/lh-fixture`, and `/lh-status` only. That gap is why the broken attach command wiring escaped unit coverage.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Import mapping depends on a synthetic `sessionManager` adapter in production code
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `importRuntimeContext()` in `src/context-steward/services/import-service.ts:112-130` builds a synthetic `sessionManager` with stubbed methods such as `getLeafId: () => null`, `getEntry: () => undefined`, and `getBranch: () => []` solely to satisfy `mapPiMessageEnd()`. I did not reproduce a current failure from this because the mapper currently reads session id/file-path metadata only, but it is a brittle production-path adapter that will silently fall out of sync if the mapper starts depending on more session-manager behavior.

unresolvedItems: The lifecycle fix still needs an explicit rule for deciding, on `session_start` and `session_before_switch`, when a target session is brand-new and safe to auto-manage versus already populated and requiring attach/import.

`/lh-attach` still needs a settled command contract for session-path versus session-identifier inputs, including which target metadata should win when the operator points at a session other than the current live context.
The epic gate needs an explicit enforcement decision: add the planned `file-thread-store.integration.test.ts` suite, make zero discovered integration tests fail fast, or both.

crossStoryFindings: Story 5's attach/import contract is undercut by Story 2's PI lifecycle wiring: the extension auto-manages any newly seen session target before an explicit attach can import prior history.

Story 7's PI-session fixture path is branch-aware, but Story 5's operator attach path is not; `executeFixtureCommand` forwards `activeLeafId` and the live `sessionManager`, while `executeAttachCommand` omits both.

The test suite is green, but it currently protects the wrong session-switch behavior: `tests/context-steward/capture-service.test.ts:741-770` asserts that a fresh managed thread should be created whenever the session target changes.
architectureFindings: `src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:563-617` violates `docs/spec-build/technical-architecture.md:372-375` by calling `openOrCreateManagedThread()` for every session/message event, instead of requiring attach/import before treating a pre-populated session as managed.

`src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:304-320` violates the active-path contract in `docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/tech-design.md:62-63`: `/lh-attach` does not route the live `SessionManager.getBranch()` / current leaf context into import, so branch-aware attach differs from the designed command behavior.
epicCoverageAssessment: `npm run verify` passed with 104 unit tests, so most store/capture/repair behaviors are exercised at the service level.

Epic coverage is incomplete: `docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/test-plan.md:221-235` requires `verify-all` integration coverage through `file-thread-store.integration.test.ts`, but the repository has no `*.integration.test.ts` files and `npm run verify-all` ended with `No integration tests found.`

Command-level coverage drift contributed directly to escaped bugs: `tests/context-steward/pi-extension-commands.test.ts` covers fixture/status only, while the plan also calls for `/lh-attach`, `/lh-turn-health`, and `/lh-repair-turns` command tests.
productionPathFindings: Reproduced a real entrypoint failure: after a `session_start` event on a pre-populated PI session, the extension created a managed thread containing only a `runtime_event`, and a subsequent `/lh-attach` failed with `TARGET_ASSOCIATION_CONFLICT`, so prior history could no longer be imported.

Reproduced a real attach-path failure: on a branched live session, `/lh-attach` returned `IMPORT_PATH_AMBIGUOUS` even though the live session manager exposed a unique active leaf/branch; the fixture command succeeds in the same situation because it forwards the live manager.

The only notable non-real path is verification: `scripts/run-node-tests.mjs:41-43` exits successfully when zero integration tests are present, so `verify-all` can pass without the planned integration smoke coverage.

blockingFindings.title: PI lifecycle events auto-manage existing sessions before attach/import can preserve prior history
blockingFindings.evidence: `src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:563-617` always resolves a managed thread via `openOrCreateManagedThread()` before handling `session_start`, `session_before_switch`, `session_shutdown`, `turn_start`, `turn_end`, or `message_end`. Repro: emitting `session_start` for a pre-populated session created a managed thread whose only stored message was `runtime_event`, and a following `/lh-attach` returned `TARGET_ASSOCIATION_CONFLICT` (`PI target session-existing is already managed by thread ...`). That blocks the import path required by `docs/spec-build/technical-architecture.md:372-375` and loses the prior source history that AC-5 depends on.

blockingFindings.title: `/lh-attach` is wired to the wrong target and ignores the live active-branch context
blockingFindings.evidence: `src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:304-320` parses command args only into `sessionFilePath` and then calls `attachExistingPiSession()` with `targetFromContext(ctx)`. It never forwards `activeLeafIdFromContext()` or `importSessionManagerFromContext()`, even though `executeFixtureCommand` does at `src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:449-457`. Repro 1: `/lh-attach` on a branched live session failed with `IMPORT_PATH_AMBIGUOUS` although the live `sessionManager` exposed a unique leaf/branch. Repro 2: `/lh-attach <other-session-file>` imported 1 message but created a managed thread targeted at the current session id/file instead of the requested file, so imported history was bound to the wrong live session.

blockingFindings.title: Epic gate passes vacuously because the planned integration test layer does not exist
blockingFindings.evidence: `docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/test-plan.md:221-235` says `verify-all` must run integration smoke coverage via `file-thread-store.integration.test.ts`, but the repository has no `*.integration.test.ts` files. `scripts/run-node-tests.mjs:31-43` exits 0 when the integration file list is empty, and `node scripts/run-node-tests.mjs integration` printed `No integration tests found.` This means the epic gate is not exercising the promised process-reopen/import/concurrency integration path.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Planned command coverage is missing for attach, turn-health, and repair commands
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/test-plan.md:175-185` lists `/lh-attach`, `/lh-turn-health`, `/lh-repair-turns`, `/lh-fixture`, and `/lh-status` command tests, but `tests/context-steward/pi-extension-commands.test.ts:88-222` only exercises fixture and status flows. That left the broken attach wiring unprotected at the command layer.

unresolvedItems: The fix needs a clear rule for distinguishing a brand-new session from an existing populated session when `session_start` or a session switch fires, so the extension knows when to auto-open/create versus when to require explicit attach/import.
The `/lh-attach` argument contract needs to be nailed down in code and tests: today args are treated as a file path only, but the spec allows session path or session identifier.

crossStoryFindings: The PI-session fixture flow and the `/lh-attach` command have drifted apart: fixture creation passes the live `SessionManager` and active leaf into import, but attach does not, so the same branched session can succeed in one story surface and fail in another.
Story-level unit coverage is broad, but the epic-level release gate no longer exercises the planned cross-process/file-layout integration checks because there are no `.integration.test.ts` files.
architectureFindings: The tech design requires active-path selection from `SessionManager.getBranch()` on the current leaf (`docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/tech-design.md:62-63`), but `executeAttachCommand` calls `attachExistingPiSession` without `activeLeafId` or `sessionManager` (`src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:304-320`).

The test plan defines `verify-all` as the epic completion gate and names four filesystem/import smoke tests (`docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/test-plan.md:221-235`), but the current runner exits 0 when the integration suite is empty (`scripts/run-node-tests.mjs:31-43`).
epicCoverageAssessment: `npm run verify` passed with 104 unit tests covering store, capture, import, repair, fixtures, and extension helper flows.

Epic coverage is still incomplete at the production boundary: the planned integration file `file-thread-store.integration.test.ts` is absent, and `/lh-attach` on a branched live session is not covered.

Because `npm run verify-all` currently runs no integration tests, process-style reopen/import smoke coverage, file-path import coverage, queue serialization under integration conditions, and stale temp-file crash cleanup are only validated by unit-level harnesses.
productionPathFindings: The release gate is currently a non-real execution path: `npm run verify-all` passed after printing `No integration tests found.` because the integration runner treats an empty suite as success.

The import pipeline uses a fabricated `sessionManager` adapter in production code (`src/context-steward/services/import-service.ts:112-130`) with stubbed methods like `getBranch: () => []` and `getEntry: () => undefined`; it works only because `mapPiMessageEnd` currently reads session id/file path only.

The real `/lh-attach` production path does not use the live `SessionManager` at all, so branched-session attach behavior differs from the real-session fixture path that does pass the live manager (`src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:449-457`).

blockingFindings.title: `/lh-attach` ignores the live session manager and cannot attach the active branch of a branched PI session
blockingFindings.evidence: `executeAttachCommand` forwards only `store`, `target`, `sessionFilePath`, and `now` to `attachExistingPiSession` (`src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:304-320`), while the fixture command correctly passes `activeLeafId` and `sessionManager` (`src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:449-457`). The design says active-path resolution must come from `SessionManager.getBranch()` on the current leaf (`docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/tech-design.md:62-63`). I reproduced this through the registered `lh-attach` handler against a branched session fixture: the command returned `IMPORT_PATH_AMBIGUOUS ... expected exactly one leaf candidate but found 2` instead of importing the live branch.

blockingFindings.title: `verify-all` is a hollow gate because the integration suite is missing and the runner treats zero tests as success
blockingFindings.evidence: The test plan defines `verify-all` as `npm run verify && npm run test:integration` and explicitly calls for `file-thread-store.integration.test.ts` smoke coverage (`docs/spec-build/epics/01-session-context-store/test-plan.md:221-235`). `package.json` wires that gate exactly (`package.json:14-17`), but `scripts/run-node-tests.mjs` exits 0 when no matching integration files exist (`scripts/run-node-tests.mjs:39-43`). In this repo there are no `*.integration.test.ts` files under `tests/`, and `npm run verify-all` completed with the final output `No integration tests found.`

nonBlockingFindings.title: Import mapping depends on a fabricated `sessionManager` shim in production code
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: `importRuntimeContext` constructs a synthetic context with stubbed session-manager methods such as `getLeafId: () => null`, `getBranch: () => []`, and `getEntry: () => undefined` solely to satisfy `mapPiMessageEnd` (`src/context-steward/services/import-service.ts:112-130`). This is not breaking today, but it is a brittle non-real adapter in the production path.
